summary.problem: A typo in a policy rule property name (e.g., toolname instead of toolName) is silently stripped during parsing, causing the rule to match all tools and inadvertently allow all tools.
summary.root_cause: In packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts, PolicyRuleSchema and SafetyCheckerRuleSchema use Zod z.object() without .strict(). Zod silently strips unrecognized keys by default, leaving toolName as undefined, which the policy engine interprets as matching all tools.
summary.context: Rejecting policy entries with unexpected or misspelled fields prevents silent configuration errors that could lead to unintended tool permission grants.

steps: In packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts, append .strict() to PolicyRuleSchema so that any unrecognized keys in policy rules trigger a Zod schema validation error.
In packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts, append .strict() to SafetyCheckerRuleSchema so that any unrecognized keys in safety checker rules trigger a Zod schema validation error.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Policy files containing unrecognized or misspelled keys (e.g., toolname) fail schema validation and result in a schema_validation error.
verification_steps: Add a unit test in packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.test.ts that attempts to load a policy TOML containing unknown keys like toolname.
Assert that loadPoliciesFromToml returns zero rules and records a schema_validation error.
Run the test suite using Vitest to verify all tests pass.

github_metadata.title: Typo in policy inadvertently allows all tools
